FINDINGS:

The proposal depends on age-based log retention, but that is not the current policy in this snapshot. `app/db.py:add_log` inserts immutable rows; `cleanup_old_logs()` raises an error, and `app/manager.py:start_background_tasks()` says log retention was removed. Rows can be deleted through the `logs.session_id` foreign key when a session is deleted (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). There is no blob store or log-linked file cleanup in the inspected code. Keeping blobs “as long as log retention keeps the row” therefore has no defined age boundary today.

Image results do not all have the same representation. `app/backend_claude.py:_extract_tool_result()` stringifies result blocks, and `app/session.py:_handle_event` (the event handler containing the `tool_result` case) logs the resulting `event.content` unchanged. Codex `imageView` results in `app/backend_codex.py` contain a `file_path`, while `_result_text()` serializes text blocks and truncates to 20,000 characters. The frontend detects base64 image data in tool results and renders it; for Read results it can instead fetch the original file through `/api/files/raw`. Telegram also tries to send the original Read image file. These paths show that source paths may be referenced separately from encoded image content; they do not establish that all 52 alleged rows contain the same kind of payload or a stable path.

The claimed 52 rows and 43% concentration cannot be checked here: this snapshot contains no SQLite database or image files. I therefore cannot verify row count, byte totals, whether “bytes” means UTF-8 encoded journal content or decoded image size, referenced-file availability, duplicates, shared paths, or whether source files changed. The frontend’s 16,000-byte cap and comments about large base64 rows corroborate the general storage and transfer concern, not those specific figures.

Copying a file during `add_log` would not by itself provide safe row-to-blob lifetime management. Shared or duplicate references require deduplication and reference counts (or mark-and-sweep); deleting one row must not remove a blob still used by another. A source can disappear or change between event creation and copy. Copy failure, DB failure after copy, and concurrent writes/deletes can leave missing references or orphaned blobs. Current asynchronous `_log()` submits writes to a DB executor and logs failures; it does not make filesystem and SQLite changes atomic. A retention cleanup would need coordinated deletion, retries, and reconciliation. Since rows currently persist indefinitely, copying base64 payloads into blobs could add storage without reducing journal size unless the row format is also changed.

Recommendation: do not adopt the proposal as phrased. First measure the live database and verify each candidate payload and source path. If reducing SQLite size is the goal, design an explicit content-addressed blob scheme with transactional references and a reconciliation process; define retention only if policy changes, and preserve image readability when source files are unavailable. Until then, the snapshot supports concern about large image results, but not the reported 43% measurement or the proposed retention behavior.
